{{Short description|German-Swedish molecular biophysicist, biochemist, and structural biologist}}

'''Sebastian Deindl''' (born March 16, 1978 in [[Basel]]) is a German-Swedish [[Biochemistry|biochemist]], molecular [[Biophysics|biophysicist]] and  [[Structural biology|structural biologist]]. In November 2024, Sebastian Deindl was selected for an [[Alexander von Humboldt Professorship|Alexander von Humboldt professorship]].<ref name="Humboldt">{{cite web|access-date=2025-01-11 |language=de |title=Sebastian Deindl |type=Alexander von Humboldt-Professur 2025 |url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/entdecken/newsroom/dossier-alexander-von-humboldt-professur/sebastian-deindl |website=humboldt-foundation.de}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

== Education and career ==
Sebastian Deindl studied [[biochemistry]] at the [[:de:Eberhard Karls Universität Tübingen|University of Tübingen]], where he became familiar with structural biology. He completed his degree in 2004 with a diploma. In 2009, he earned his Ph.D. at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], under the supervision of [[John Kuriyan]].<ref name="Humboldt2">{{cite web|access-date=2025-01-11 |language=de |title=Sebastian Deindl |type=Alexander von Humboldt-Professur 2025 |url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/entdecken/newsroom/dossier-alexander-von-humboldt-professur/sebastian-deindl |website=humboldt-foundation.de}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref name=":02">{{cite web|access-date=2025-01-12 |language=en |publisher=deindl-lab |title=Sebastian Deindl Short CV |url=https://deindl-lab.com/CV}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> During this time, his research focused on the biophysical mechanisms of signal transduction and the structure of protein complexes.

After completing his Ph.D., Deindl worked from 2009 to 2014 as a Jane Coffin Childs postdoctoral fellow<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2025-01-13 |author=Alison Fromme |date=2013-10-01 |title=Research & Achievements (2013) |url=https://www.jccfund.org/blog/research-and-achievements-2013/}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> at the Department of Chemistry and Chemical Biology at [[Harvard University]], where he was part of [[Xiaowei Zhuang]]'s research group. There, he developed [[Single-molecule experiment|single-molecule]] techniques and applied them to the study of [[:de:Chromatin|chromatin]] dynamics.<ref name=":03">{{cite web|access-date=2025-01-12 |language=en |publisher=deindl-lab |title=Sebastian Deindl Short CV |url=https://deindl-lab.com/CV}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

In 2014, Deindl assumed an assistant professorship at [[Uppsala University]]. He was promoted to associate professor in 2018 and appointed full professor of Molecular Biophysics in 2021.<ref name="Humboldt3">{{cite web|access-date=2025-01-11 |language=de |title=Sebastian Deindl |type=Alexander von Humboldt-Professur 2025 |url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/entdecken/newsroom/dossier-alexander-von-humboldt-professur/sebastian-deindl |website=humboldt-foundation.de}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> At Uppsala University, he leads a research group in the field of mechanistic chromatin biology,<ref name="uu2">{{cite web|access-date=2025-01-12 |language=en |title=Deindl lab |url=https://www.uu.se/en/department/cell-and-molecular-biology/research/molecular-biophysics/deindl-lab |website=Uppsala University |date=6 May 2024 }}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> which investigates the complex molecular structures and dynamics of nucleic acid-binding proteins and their collective |url=https://www.uu.se/en/department/cell-and-molecular-biology/research/molecular-biophysics/deindl-lab |website=Uppsala University |date=6 May 2024 }}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 |title=Humboldt-Professuren locken Spitzenforscher nach Deutschland |url=https://www.heise.de/news/Humboldt-Professuren-locken-Spitzenforscher-nach-Deutschland-218007.html |website=heise |date=8 May
